title: Towards Explainable Harmful Meme Detection through Multimodal Debate between Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect harmful multimodal memes and generate human-readable rationales explaining their harmfulness. In the context of religion, it evaluates whether the models can correctly identify, contextualize, and explain hatefulness or offensiveness directed at specific religious groups, and analyzes potential model biases (e.g., falsely classifying benign content about Muslims as harmful due to training exposure).
findings: The LLMs (LLaVA and ChatGPT) demonstrated an ability to reason well about offensiveness and hatefulness targeting religious groups using commonsense knowledge, successfully explaining harmful memes that target Christian and Jewish communities. However, the models exhibited bias in some cases: due to exposure to harmful content targeting religion during training, the models developed a tendency to incorrectly label benign content related to Muslims as harmful.
